Nothing states how the PhenoAge coefficients were sourced or checked, and no validation cohort, sample size or error bar is described for the biological-age output.

one_line: A biological-age dashboard that parses lab PDFs with Gemini into validated schemas, runs the Levine PhenoAge clock over wearable streams, and returns a weekly three-item intervention list.

sections.accomplishments: They report over 95% accuracy parsing un-standardised blood-panel PDFs into structured inputs without human intervention, a two-tap onboarding that connects the native feeds and immediately shows a chronological-versus-biological baseline, and a dashboard aesthetic borrowed from finance apps.
sections.challenges: Lab PDFs differ by provider (Quest, LabCorp, local clinics) in units and layout, which they addressed with grammar-constrained decoding so the model must emit a strict schema. Wearable HRV and resting heart rate are volatile day to day, so 7-day and 30-day exponentially weighted moving averages smooth the inputs and stop the score from jumping. Recomputing the model while drawing trend graphs pushed them to move the maths into lightweight on-device utility modules.
sections.how_we_built_it: Marketed as a longevity dashboard: it claims to translate clinical biomarker algorithms into an actionable score, “quantify, gamify, and actively reverse” aging. Built as React Native with NativeWind and Tailwind for the client, interactive 30-day, 90-day and one-year trend graphs. Gemini 1.5 Flash via Google Cloud parses multi-page lab PDFs into validated JSON schemas. The core algorithm is the Levine PhenoAge model: nine biomarkers (albumin, creatinine, glucose, hs-CRP, lymphocyte percentage, mean corpuscular volume, red cell distribution width, alkaline phosphatase, white blood cell count) mapped to a mortality-risk score through a Gompertz distribution. Node.js services on Cloud Run with Firestore for documents and live sync.
sections.inspiration: Chronological age counts Earth's rotations; biological age is meant to describe the functional state of physiology. Consumer health data arrives fragmented - HealthKit metrics, continuous glucose monitors, periodic blood panels - with no single number a person can act on. Their premise is that tracking healthspan should feel as legible as managing a portfolio, so clinical aging-clock maths becomes a dynamic score with a trend line. Their framing is explicit about the ambition: translate clinical biomarker algorithms into a score so a person can "quantify, gamify, and actively reverse" their biological aging curve.
sections.learned: Aging clocks respond more to systemic inflammatory markers such as hs-CRP than to raw daily activity, so combining a blood panel with passive streams yields a steadier model than either alone. Presenting a short prioritised intervention list drives adherence where raw medical data overwhelms users.
sections.what_it_does: Passive biometric sync pulls resting heart rate, HRV, VO2 max, sleep architecture and daily steps from HealthKit or Google Health Connect. A multimodal parser reads un-standardised lab PDFs and blood panels (HbA1c, hs-CRP, lipid profile, albumin, alkaline phosphatase) into structured biomarker values. A clock engine computes a biological age and compares it with the chronological baseline. A weekly Longevity Delta loop names the user's biometric bottleneck and returns three targeted lifestyle, protocol or supplement interventions. Monthly Wrapped-style proof cards are generated for sharing.
sections.what_next: Predictive intervention modelling - simulating how a 10% increase in deep sleep or a 15mg reduction in hs-CRP shifts the curve 90 days out - plus direct integrations with continuous glucose monitors and epigenetic testing providers.

testing: The one quantified result - over 95% PDF parsing accuracy - has no denominator: no document count, no provider breakdown, no definition of what counts as correct extraction, and no held-out set. No test suite, repo, or eval harness is linked anywhere on the page, and no clinical or statistical validation is claimed for the age score itself.
